questions.stem: Using the formula F = BIL, what is the force on a wire carrying 4 A of current with a length of 0.25 m in a magnetic field of 0.3 T?
questions.explanation: Using F = BIL: F = 0.3 x 4 x 0.25 = 0.3 N. Always ensure that the current and field are perpendicular to each other for this formula to apply directly.

questions.stem: When is the force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field zero?

options.text: When the wire is perpendicular to the field
When the wire is parallel to the field
When the current is at maximum
When the magnetic field is very strong

questions.explanation: The force on a current-carrying wire in a magnetic field is zero when the wire is parallel to the field. The force is maximum when the wire is perpendicular to the field, because there is no component of the current crossing the field lines.
